ONE DSD EQUITY TEAM · REFERENCE DOCUMENT
The Equity Cascade: DHS → ADSA → DSD
A crosswalk showing how the DHS Equity Outcome Map (enterprise framework) translates through the ADSA Implementation Plan (administration strategy) into the DSD Equity and Inclusion Operational Plan (division execution).

Why this matters. The three documents in your packet are one connected line of work — designed to translate enterprise-wide equity commitments at DHS into administration-level strategy at ADSA, and finally into the day-to-day operations of DSD staff and leaders.
How to read this. Each tier below shows what that level of the organization owns. The crosswalk table at the end maps the five strategic alignments, so any DSD action can be traced back to the ADSA commitment it satisfies and the DHS outcome it advances. Hold onto this for your own reference.

THEORY OF CHANGE
IF DHS centers equity in all work and operations — policies, program integrity, contracts, projects, workforce development, community engagement, trainings, performance plans —
————   THEN   ————

CENTERING EQUITY FOR DHS
•  Equity is centered in everyday thinking, work, and operations
•  Achievements survive leadership changes
•  Staff can bring their full selves to work

CENTERING EQUITY FOR MINNESOTANS
•  Public funds reach those who need them most
•  Disparities in health and social determinants reduced
•  Policies combat systemic oppression

CONTINUOUS LEARNING CYCLE
•  Staff feel safe seeking feedback
•  Resources to learn and grow
•  Leaders treat equity as a core competency

COMMUNITY IN PLANNING & SOLUTIONS
•  Culturally responsive, accessible engagement
•  Community engaged in ways they understand
•  Input shapes processes and program design

WHAT ADSA OWNS
ADSA sets the strategies — the goals, action steps, and guidelines that translate DHS-wide equity commitments into priorities for the administration. ADSA also leads Tribal Consultation on behalf of the administration, with DSD collaboration and input on division-relevant matters. ADSA requires each of its divisions to organize equity work around five strategic themes.

OBJECTIVE — ELIMINATE INEQUITIES IN THREE AREAS
The DSD plan translates ADSA strategy into specific, measurable actions for staff and leadership. Identifying and removing biases is treated as a core part of how we operate.

GOVERNANCE — ONE DSD EQUITY TEAM & UNIT EQUITY CHAMPIONS
DSD operates a single, division-wide One DSD Equity Team that plans, coordinates, and tracks accountability for the work. Each DSD unit designates an Equity Champion (or representative) to serve on or report into the One DSD Equity Team — ensuring every unit has a named voice and point of contact in the division-wide structure.

THE SIX OPERATIONAL GOALS
The plan executes work across six goals, each with process steps, responsible parties, timelines, and clear implications for daily work.

OUR CORE RESPONSIBILITIES — EVERY STAFF MEMBER
Four commitments held by everyone, regardless of role.

THE ACCOUNTABILITY LOOP — QUARTERLY REPORTING & CORRECTION PLANS
Equity Champions and Goal leads report progress on disparity targets to division leadership quarterly through the One DSD Equity Team. Programs showing gaps are required to present a correction plan with specific operational changes, named owners, due dates, and the metrics that will be measured in the next quarter. This is the mechanism that turns plan into practice.

Five-Point Alignment Crosswalk
How each DHS outcome flows through an ADSA requirement and lands as a specific DSD operational practice. Read each row left-to-right.

One way to use this. When you read the DSD plan section assigned to you, trace it upward through the crosswalk: which ADSA requirement does it satisfy, and which DHS outcome does it advance? If the line back doesn't hold, that's a signal worth raising. The cascade only works when every operational step connects cleanly to the enterprise commitment above it — and that traceability is what gives this plan its accountability.
